back_translation: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt, against the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was at the Euphrates River at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
Prepare the small shield and the large shield, and advance for battle!
Harness the horses; mount the steeds; take your positions with helmets on; polish the spears; put on the coats of mail!
Why do I see this? They are terrified and retreating; their warriors are beaten down; they flee in haste without looking back—terror on every side! declares the LORD.
The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape; in the north, by the River Euphrates, they stumble and fall.
Who is this that rises like the Nile, whose waters churn like the rivers?
Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like the rivers; and it says, I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.
Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots! Let the warriors go forth—Cush and Put who handle the shield, and the men of Lud who draw the bow.

For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. The sword will devour and be sated, and drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord GOD of Hosts holds a sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and get balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt! In vain you use many remedies; there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry fills the earth, for warrior has stumbled against warrior; the two of them have fallen together.
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
Announce it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes; say, Take your position and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured those around you.
Why have your strong ones been swept away? They did not stand, for the LORD thrust them down.
He made many stumble; indeed, they fell over one another, and said, Get up, let us return to our own people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.
There they cried out, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by.
As I live, declares the King—the LORD of Hosts is his name—one will come like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.
Make for yourself baggage for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt! For Memphis will become a desolation, laid waste, without inhabitant.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming, it is coming.
Even her mercenaries in her midst are like fattened calves; they too have turned and fled together; they did not stand, for the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound goes out like a serpent's, for they advance in force; with axes they come against her like woodcutters.
They chop down her forest, declares the LORD, though it is impenetrable, for they are more numerous than locusts and cannot be counted.
The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame; she will be given into the hand of the people of the north.
The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Behold, I am about to punish Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh, and Egypt with her gods and her kings—Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

And I will deliver them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. But afterward it will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.

But you, O Jacob my servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel; for behold, I will save you from afar, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be quiet and at ease, with no one to make him afraid.

You, O Jacob my servant, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you. Though I make a full end of all the nations to which I have banished you, I will not make a full end of you; but I will discipline you justly, and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
